title: Multi-Turn Interaction
content:
Many complex problems cannot be solved in a single turn. LLM agents need to interact with the environment to obtain useful feedback from other models or tools involved in the system.
Multi-Turn MAGRPO# MAGRPO in the multi-turn setting forms a tree-structured rollout expansion where branches represent different joint responses (TreeRPO).
Joint rollout tree Joint observations and actions branch into independent rollouts. Complete diagram Play Replay In each episode, a task is sampled from the dataset to construct initial observations \( \mathbf{o}_0=\{o_{1, 0}, \cdots, o_{n, 0}\} \) and histories \( \mathbf{h}_0=\{h_{1, 0}, \cdots, h_{n, 0}\} \) for all agents. At each turn, agents generate a group of joint responses \( \mathbf{a}^{\mathcal{G}}_t\gets\boldsymbol{\pi}^{\mathcal{G}}(\cdot|\mathbf{h}_t) \) from their current observation-action history \( \mathbf{h}_t \), with each response initiating a distinct rollout. Agents receive joint rewards \( r^{(g)}_{t} \) for each response based on the accumulated history \( \mathbf{a}^{(g)}_{t} \in \mathbf{a}^{\mathcal{G}}_{t} \) and current action. Each rollout then evolves independently, producing new joint observations \( \mathbf{o}^{\mathcal{G}}_{t+1} \) as the environment dynamics unfold and spawning more rollouts at the next turn \( t+1 \). This process continues until the terminal turn is reached \( H \).
Joint Mode# MAGRPO supports two modes for forming joint responses at each turn:
Aligned (joint_mode="aligned"): Combines the responses with the same generation index across agents. Each agent samples the fixed num_generations value \( G \) at every node. With \( T \) turns and no early termination, the tree has \( G^T \) leaves. Aligned joint responses Responses with matching generation indices are combined across agents. Complete diagram Play Replay Cross (joint_mode="cross"): Evaluates the Cartesian product of the agents’ sampled responses, yielding \( G^N \) joint actions per node. With no early termination, the tree has \( G^{N \cdot T} \) leaves. Responses are reused across combinations, so these are not independent joint samples. This increases reward evaluations and rollout size; it does not guarantee more accurate value estimates. Cross joint responses The Cartesian product forms joint responses within each rollout. Complete diagram Play Replay Note that only responses originating from the same rollout can be combined, as rollouts evolve independently. The current MAGRPO implementation accumulates undiscounted returns: discount does not change its tree recursion. See MA-REINFORCE for return aggregation and advantage normalization.
Multi-Turn MAAC/IAC# Different from MAGRPO rollout tree that generates numerous samples in each episode, MAAC/IAC with multi-turn training only generates one sample per agent at each turn in the multi-turning setting, and the episode continues for multiple turns until termination. MAAC/IAC use one-step temporal-difference targets, with discount applied to the next rollout value and no bootstrap after the final or early-terminated turn. The current implementation collects the full episode first, then buffers its samples and updates when rollout_buffer_size is reached (or flushes the remaining buffer at epoch end). It does not update policies between turns of the same episode. The external feedback mechanism controls how environment observations are incorporated into prompts for subsequent turns, which is usually implemented in CoMLRL’s downstreaming environments.
Actor-critic trajectory One joint response per turn advances the episode from left to right. Complete diagram Play Replay Environment Transition# External feedback mechanisms control how environment observations are incorporated into prompts for subsequent turns, this is usually implemented in CoMLRL’s downstreaming environments.
Custom External Feedback# Users can implement custom external feedback by defining a function with the following interface:
External Feedback Parameters prompt: Original task prompt/problem description (required) agent_completions: List or tuple of completions from the previous turn, one per agent (required) num_agents: Number of agents in the system (required) prompt_history_per_agent: List of prompt histories for each agent, where each history is a list of prompts from previous turns (optional) response_history_per_agent: List of response histories for each agent, where each history is a list of responses from previous turns (optional) The function must return a list or tuple of prompts for the next turn, one for each agent. The trainer only passes the arguments above (no extra kwargs), so any mode-specific parameters should be captured via closure or functools.partial.
By default, returned prompts are inserted as the new prompt field and then passed through each agent’s formatter. If external_prompt_passthrough=true, the returned prompts are used directly without re-formatting. In MAGRPO, the external transition is called per rollout branch with that branch’s histories.
For example:
from typing import List, Optional def custom_external( prompt: str, agent_completions: List[str], num_agents: int, prompt_history_per_agent: Optional[List[List[str]]] = None, response_history_per_agent: Optional[List[List[str]]] = None, ) -> List[str]: # Custom logic to format next-turn prompts # Access environment feedback, tool outputs, etc. next_turn_prompts = [] for i in range(num_agents): # Format prompt for agent i based on history and feedback next_prompt = f"{prompt}\nPrevious attempt: {agent_completions[i]}\nPlease revise." next_turn_prompts.append(next_prompt) return next_turn_prompts For IAC/MAAC multi-turn training, num_generations must be set to 1.
Example Modes (Expert, Diagnosis, and Self-Improvement)# An environment for code generation includes 3 example external transition modes:
external.mode=expert_edits: Uses an external LLM (default: DeepSeek-Coder) to propose code edits. Follow-up prompts include edit suggestions with context from previous turns. It can be configured via expert_model for different experts (e.g., Claude, GPT) when API keys are available.
external.mode=level_feedback: Static AST checks and dynamically executes code to provide diagnosis. The default sandbox test includes the first test; configurable via sandbox_slice to include all tests (0, None, or ‘all’), specific number of tests (negative values enabled).
external.mode=plain: Self-improvement mode that just includes prompts and responses in the previous turns and a revision instruction.
For actor/comparator layouts and centralized preference training, see Training Paradigms. Remote comparator configuration is covered in Comparator.

title: Training Parallelization
content:
CoMLRL trainers run in a Python process. For IAC, parallel_training="none" is the default; "mp" enables scheduling agents and critics on explicitly assigned devices. Neither mode requires a job scheduler.
Model Parallelization# Pass an IACConfig to your IACTrainer through its args parameter. For example, with four visible CUDA devices and two agents:
from comlrl.trainers.actor_critic import IACConfig config = IACConfig( num_agents=2, num_turns=1, use_separate_critic=True, parallel_training="mp", agent_devices=["cuda:0", "cuda:1"], critic_devices=["cuda:2", "cuda:3"], )agent_devices is required in "mp" mode. critic_devices is also required when use_separate_critic=True. Each model stays on its assigned device; this does not split an individual model across GPUs. Responses are passed to the reward function and rewards are used for each agent’s update.
Device indices refer to the GPUs visible to the Python process. Configure the device lists to match your machine and the memory needed by each model. Changing device placement or parallel scheduling can change numerical training results.

title: Developer

Support# We are willing to help you with any issues you encounter while using CoMLRL.
Report Issues# If you are stuck with a problem using CoMLRL, please follow this procedure:
Read the documentation first, including using the search feature (Ctrl + K).
Search the GitHub Issues archives to see if someone else already had the same problem.
Before writing, try to create a minimal example that reproduces the problem. You’ll get the fastest response if you can send just a handful of lines of code that show what isn’t working.
Contributing# Thanks for your interest in helping build CoMLRL! This guide walks you through reporting issues, contributing changes, and keeping the codebase healthy.
